thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1777777777 - Elevated 5xx & timeouts observed through gateway. 5xx rate jumped from 0.3% -> 6.9% in last 3m. P95 latency for text-generation is 2.4s (normal 400ms). batching-scheduler queue depth spiked to 92k items.

alice: Paging oncall: I'm oncall for infra, jumping in. Which region is noisy?

sam: us-west-2 primarily. Request rate from a few high-throughput customers increased ~6x starting ~10:08 UTC. Many long sequences -> big KV caches, batching buildup.

tess: Confirmed: batcher backlog shows steady accumulation on scheduler pool-3. Head-of-line blocking — small numbers of large requests are holding batches open.

maria: Logs show gateway 504 and internal 502s, and gateway-nginx upstream timeouts to runtime pods. Tokenize CPU usage on runtime nodes also spiking.

alice: Assigning remediation steps: 1) throttle the offending customer routes 2) open emergency routing to spare capacity 3) reduce max batch window 4) evict oldest requests if necessary.

jeff: Support reports customers A/42 and B/17 seeing elevated 504s on generation endpoints (chat.complete). They're in us-west-2.

sam: Running quick query to identify offending clients:
```
SELECT client_id, count(*) as q, avg(seq_len) FROM requests
WHERE ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY client_id ORDER BY q desc LIMIT 10;
```

sam: Top noisy client is client-prod-merchant (client_id: c-prod-009) - long prompts + streaming turned off.

tess: On the runtime side I'm scaling up spare workers in us-west-2 and nuking the largest KV caches on a subset of nodes to free memory. Scaling request sent (autoscaler).

alice: While scaling finishes, let's reduce the batching window globally to lower latency and reduce HOL impact. tess, can you patch scheduler config?

tess: Patching now. Command: `kubectl apply -f scheduler-config.yaml` with change `batch_window_ms: 10 -> 2` and `max_batch_tokens: 4096 -> 2048`.

deploy-bot: deploy started: patch/scheduler-config (run id d-1777).

maria: Also toggling a temporary routing policy to split traffic away from overloaded runtime pool-3 to pool-1: `route set --region us-west-2 --policy spillover:pool-1`.

jeff: Notifying affected customers: sent initial status to A/42 and B/17. Asking for any outstanding long-running requests.

sam: Additional mitigation: disabling request coalescing on the gateway for chat.complete endpoints to avoid cross-request HOL. Exec: `gatewayctl set-coalesce false --route chat.complete`

alice: If these don't stabilize in 5 minutes, we should evict oldest queued requests in scheduler by age > 45s and return 429 with retry-after to upstream consumers. Agree?

tess: Agree. Prepping eviction command: `schedulerctl evict --age 45s --reason hol-eviction --dry-run=false`

maria: Observability: creating a temporary dashboard for batch-queue-depth, per-client pending-requests, and KV-cache-size. Adding alerts at 50k and 80k.

sam: After the config patch, queue depth dropped to 47k and 5xx down to 2.1% within 90s. P95 falling to ~900ms.

jeff: Support update: customers reporting significant improvement, 504s decreasing. Sending note: "We've applied routing and batching mitigations; monitoring closely; follow-up PM will send postmortem."

alice: OK, continue monitoring. Next: create incident ticket (INC-1777) with root-cause hypothesis: large-sequence heavy client plus batching window + KV growth causing HOL blocking -> gateway timeouts.

sam: Adding runbook items: - rate-limit high seq clients - set per-client batch caps - ensure streaming enabled for heavy clients - autoscale KV cache eviction policy threshold.

tess: We'll keep reduced batch_window for now and schedule a gradual rollout of adaptive batch windows that shrink for high-variance sequences.

maria: Postmortem owners: sam (diagnostics), tess (runtime fix), alice (capacity/SLAs), jeff (customer comms). ETA to publish: 72h.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1777 created by alice at 1777777830. Status: mitigated -> monitoring.

alice: Closing this channel for immediate action items. If we see another spike, escalate to SRE pager and consider temporarily disabling batching on the gateway.

jeff: Follow-up ticket filed in PM board with suggested client-specific throttle and docs.

sam: Note: capture heap snapshots for runtime nodes used by pool-3 before they drop out of rotation.

tess: Saved snapshots to s3://redwood-incidents/1777777777/ and attached to the incident.

maria: Leaving monitoring alarms active for 24h. Will reopen if 5xx > 1% sustained for >5m.

alice: Thanks everyone. Good job keeping customer impact low. :thumbsup:
